variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
var mutableCount = 0
mutableCount += 1

let immutableVal = 10 # Evaluated at runtime
const compileTimeVal = 20 # Evaluated at compile time
variables.notes: Nim uses `var` for mutable variables, `let` for immutable variables, and `const` for compile-time constants.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
var
  a: int = 42
  b: float = 3.14
  c: bool = true
  d: char = 'x'
  e: string = "Nim"
data_types.notes: Nim supports standard types. Variable declarations can be grouped under a single `var` or `let` block.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Nim allows operator overloading. String concatenation uses the `&` operator.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: Conditionals are indentation-based and can be used as expressions to yield a value.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.notes: Nim heavily uses iterators for loops. `..<` creates an exclusive range, while `..` creates an inclusive one.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
var i = 0
while i < 5:
  echo i
  inc i
while_loop.notes: Standard `while` loops are available. The `inc` procedure is idiomatic for incrementing variables.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
proc add(a, b: int): int =
  result = a + b # 'result' is implicitly returned

func pureAdd(a, b: int): int =
  a + b # Func enforces no side effects
functions.notes: Nim uses `proc` for procedures and `func` for side-effect-free functions. The special `result` variable can be used for implicit returns.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.notes: Fixed-size arrays use `array`. Dynamic arrays are called sequences (`seq`), constructed using the `@` prefix.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
import std/tables

var ages = {"Alice": 30, "Bob": 25}.toTable
ages["Charlie"] = 40

if ages.hasKey("Alice"):
  echo ages["Alice"]
maps.notes: Maps are called Tables and are provided by the `std/tables` module.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Nim uses traditional exception handling. Alternatively, result types (`std/options` or third-party `Result` modules) are often used for error handling.

comments.title: Comments & Documentation
comments.code:
# Single-line comment in Nim

"""
Multi-line documentation block.
Provides docstrings for functions and modules.
"""

def add(a, b):
    """Return sum of a and b."""
    return a + b
comments.notes: Nim uses # for line comments and triple quotes for multi-line documentation strings.

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Nim supports arbitrary-precision or native integers, IEEE floats, and numeric literal prefixes (0x, 0b).

booleans.title: Booleans & Conditions
booleans.code:
let is_active = true
let has_failed = false

if is_active and not has_failed:
    echo "Active"
booleans.notes: Nim represents boolean values with logical and, or, and not operators.

type_casting.title: Type Casting & Conversion
type_casting.notes: Nim uses explicit conversion functions or operators to transform types between primitives.

strings.title: Strings & Escapes
strings.code:
s1 = "Double-quoted string"
s2 = 'Single-quoted string'
raw = r"C:\new_folder\raw.txt"
multi = """Line 1
Line 2"""
strings.notes: Nim supports single, double, and raw string literals that ignore escape characters.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import strformat
let name = "Alice"
let score = 95
echo fmt"User {name} scored {score}"
string_formatting.notes: Nim uses f-string interpolation or format specifiers for embedded expression formatting.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
case val
of 1: echo "One"
of 2, 3: echo "Two or Three"
else: echo "Other"
pattern_matching.notes: Nim provides structural pattern matching with match/case or case-of expressions.

range.title: Ranges & Slices
range.notes: Nim provides built-in range generation and slicing syntax with interval boundaries.

iterators.title: Iterators & Generators
iterators.code:
iterator countdown(n: int): int =
  var x = n
  while x > 0:
    yield x
    dec x
iterators.notes: Nim uses generator functions or iterators with the yield keyword for lazy element production.

oop_classes.title: Classes & OOP
oop_classes.code:
type
  Person = ref object of RootObj
    name*: string
    age*: int

method greet(p: Person): string {.base.} =
  "Hello " & p.name
oop_classes.notes: Nim supports object-oriented paradigms with methods, constructors, and encapsulation.

lists.title: Lists & Dynamic Arrays
lists.code:
var list = @[1, 2, 3]
list.add(4)
let first = list[0]
lists.notes: Nim provides mutable dynamic lists/sequences with append, insert, and indexing operations.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.code:
let pair: (int, string) = (1, "apple")
let (x, name) = pair
tuples.notes: Nim provides immutable ordered tuples supporting unpack destructuring.

sets.title: Sets & Collections
sets.notes: Nim provides unique element set collections with membership tests and mathematical set operations.

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
import std/[strutils, os]
from math import sqrt
modules_import.notes: Nim manages code organization via modules and selective import statements.
